title: Public Data
tagline: Open datasets generated and published by the Podcast Index project.
intro: Podcast Index produces a number of public data exports - full feed catalogs, recommendation lists, value-block dumps, activity stats, and infrastructure pointers - all served as static files under public.podcastindex.org and a few sibling subdomains. They are free to mirror and use; please don't hammer them in tight loops, send a User-Agent that names your application (requests with generic or default library User-Agents, such as plain curl or python-requests, are refused with a 403), and prefer the SQLite/CSV catalog dumps over live API scraping when you need bulk data.

sections.name: Catalog snapshots
sections.description: Full feed catalogs. The SQLite dumps are the canonical bulk artifacts - load them directly with sqlite3 or any client.

datasets.name: All live feeds - SQLite
datasets.description: Every feed currently being polled, with title, URL, owner, iTunes ID, host, language, categories, generator, and lastest-episode timestamps. The most heavily used artifact downstream - most third-party mirrors of the Podcast Index data start here.

datasets.name: Dead feeds - CSV (id only)
datasets.description: Lightweight CSV of dead feed IDs and the ID of the feed they duplicate (if any). Use this if you only need to reconcile your own list of feeds against the dead set.

datasets.name: Problematic feeds - CSV
datasets.description: Dead feeds that have an entry in the problematic-feeds table. Includes feed URL, generator, author, owner, iTunes ID, the reason code, and the editor's note. Hosting-company brand names are stripped from the note column for cleaner pattern analysis.

sections.name: Discovery & recommendations
sections.description: Curated and computed lists derived from podcast 2.0 tags and feed metadata.

datasets.name: Recommendations - all media
datasets.description: Show recommendations mined from <podcast:podroll> tags across the whole index, ranked by mention count.

datasets.name: Recommendations - video only
datasets.description: The same recommendation graph, filtered to feeds whose <podcast:medium> or content profile marks them as video.

datasets.name: Recommendations - music only
datasets.description: The same recommendation graph, filtered to feeds whose <podcast:medium> or content profile marks them as music.

datasets.name: Podcast locations
datasets.description: All live feeds carrying a <podcast:location> tag, with the place name, rel type (subject or creator), OpenStreetMap object ID, ISO country code, and latitude/longitude from the tag.

datasets.name: Value-enabled feeds - CSV
datasets.description: All feeds carrying a <podcast:value> block, grouped by host. Useful for surveying Lightning/Hive value-for-value adoption across the index.

datasets.name: Hosting provider stats
datasets.description: Top hosting providers by live feed count. A quick read on the shape of the podcasting hosting market.

sections.name: Activity & stats
sections.description: Time-series counts and rolling new-feed reports.

datasets.name: 24-hour feed report - HTML
datasets.description: Human-readable daily report: counts of new feeds added in the last 24 hours, top generators, hour-by-hour add rate, and keyword-based scoring of the new-arrival mix.

datasets.name: Newly-added feeds (last 24h) - CSV
datasets.description: Sliding-window CSV of every feed added to the index in the past 24 hours. Datestamped daily snapshots are also published as newlyAddedFeeds24hoursYYYY-MM-DD.csv.

datasets.name: Hourly counts
datasets.description: Hour-bucketed aggregate counts: feeds added, episodes added, and API requests served. Useful for charting recent index activity.

datasets.name: Daily counts
datasets.description: Day-bucketed aggregate counts with a longer retention window than the hourly file - better for long-term trend lines.

sections.name: Lookalike feeds
sections.description: Pairs of live feeds that look very much like each other because they share episodes: a show copied to another host, a host migration, a same-owner mirror, or the same feed listed twice. A pair is included when the two feeds share at least 3 episode guids and at least 50% of the smaller side's newest 50 episodes. When they share no guids at all, episodes also count as shared if they have the same title, were published within 48 hours of each other and differ in length by at most 10 seconds (this catches shows re-published with fresh guids); such pairs carry the signal matched_by_titles and a confidence of at most 0.75. Pairs where both feeds are PeerTube channel feeds are left out: PeerTube federation mirrors a channel onto many instances by design. Each pair carries a likely label, a 0-1 confidence and the signals behind it. Labels are likely classifications for you to verify, not determinations. host_migration: the owner moved (redirect or itunes:new-feed-url, a shared Apple id, or the old feed went quiet under the same owner). same_owner_mirror: both feeds publishing and serving the same audio files (at least one shared episode with the identical audio URL), or with related author/owner names and the same owner email. duplicate_listing: the same feed under several urls on one host with the same podcast:guid (dropped once the Index merges them). copy: the likely original is still publishing while another feed carries its episodes with the audio re-hosted elsewhere (or made longer by inserted ads), usually under a different author or owner and its own or no Apple id. The feed's website link is not used as evidence: copies often point it back at the original. unclear: shared episodes, conflicting signals. Confidence starts at a base per label (duplicate 0.80, migration 0.55, mirror 0.50, copy 0.50, unclear 0.30) and moves 0.10 per supporting signal (copy: at most 0.75 unless the episodes are longer than the original's, then -0.15 for each of a related author/owner name or matching owner email), clamped to 0.05-0.95. Feed A is the likely original: the older Apple id, else the feed whose copies of the shared episodes we stored first, else the lower feed id (original_basis says which). Owner emails are reduced to their domain. The signals column lists every signal that fired.

datasets.name: Lookalike feeds - backlog baseline
datasets.description: Published once: every lookalike pair that was already live when the report started, the starting point for the daily files.

datasets.name: Lookalike feeds - backlog summary (HTML)
datasets.description: A readable overview of the backlog: pair counts by likely label and copy confidence, and the most popular shows with a likely copy at confidence 0.85 or higher, with links to both feeds in the Index and on Apple.

datasets.name: Lookalike feeds - all known pairs
datasets.description: Cumulative list of every pair currently known, with its current label. detected_on is when the pair was first reported; last_checked is the last time it was re-evaluated.

datasets.name: Lookalike feeds - today's new and changed pairs
datasets.description: Every pair that changed on the latest run date (changed_on): first detected (change=new), its likely label changed (change=label_changed, with previous_label), or the feed shown as the likely original flipped (change=original_changed). Feeds created in roughly the last 7 days are re-checked each day so a feed parsed late is still caught.

datasets.name: Lookalike feeds - dated daily CSVs
datasets.description: One file per run date, named lookalike_feeds_YYYY-MM-DD.csv (UTC), with the same rows as that day's daily CSV. A day's file is never changed by later runs, so you can fetch any past date to walk back through the history; a date with no run has no file. The link is an example; replace the date.

datasets.name: Lookalike feeds - today's report (HTML)
datasets.description: The same rows as today's CSV as a readable page, copies first, with links to both feeds in the Index and on Apple.

sections.name: Infrastructure feeds
sections.description: Operational pointers used by clients of the Podcast Index ecosystem.

datasets.name: Healthy Hive RPC nodes
datasets.description: Plain-text list of Hive blockchain RPC nodes that have recently passed a health check. Consumed by Podping listeners that need a working node to subscribe to.

datasets.name: Live tracking firehose - current window
datasets.description: Most recent ~200-second window of newly-added or updated feeds and items, as JSON. Polled by partner mobile apps to keep their local catalogs current. Per-window archives are also written under /<unix-timestamp>.
